Moments Matter.

A job is made of small moments: where to stand, what to watch and, most importantly, when to say stop. Our safety program is built so every person on our crews gets those moments right, and goes home the way they arrived.

Safety starts
before the work does.

Before a crew sets foot on site, they know its hazards, the client's requirements and the plan for the day. On site, the plan is checked every morning, and anyone can stop the work when something isn't right.

Before the job

Prequalification

We hold our place in ISNetworld, Avetta and Veriforce, so clients can review our safety programs and record before we arrive.

Operator Qualification

Crew members performing covered tasks on pipeline work hold current Operator Qualification for each of those tasks.

Site-specific orientation

Every crew member is walked through the site's hazards, access, emergency plan and client rules before work begins.

On the job

Daily JSA and tailgate meeting

Each day starts with a job safety analysis and a tailgate meeting: the day's tasks, the hazards in them and how we control each one.

Excavation and trenching

A competent person is on site for every excavation, inspecting the protective systems and the ground before anyone goes in.

Working near and in water

Crews at the water's edge wear flotation and keep rescue equipment at hand, and the plan accounts for water that can rise quickly.

Heavy equipment

Equipment is run only by trained, certified operators, inspected before every shift, with spotters wherever visibility is limited.

After every job

Near-miss and incident reporting

We report near misses as seriously as incidents, find out why they happened and share the lesson with every crew.

Annual required training

Every employee completes safety training specific to their role each year, updated with what our crews have learned.

Stop Work Authority

The most important moment on any job is the one where someone says stop.

Anyone on an Er-Con site, from a first-week hire to a visitor, has the authority to stop work when something isn't right. No one is questioned for using it. The work starts again when the hazard is dealt with.

Prequalifying a contractor?

Ask for our safety program.

Send us your prequalification requirements. We'll provide our safety program, our record and our certifications.
